title: A micropattern-based assay to study contact inhibition of locomotion and entosis of adherent human and canine cells in vitro
protocol: Place the micropatterned slide into a well of a 6 well tissue culture dish for easier handling when coating and washing.
Prepare coating solution with a 2× concentration of the ECM protein in PBS−/−.
For each micropatterned slide, prepare 2 ml of the 2× concentrated (20 μg/mL) coating solution.
Avoid touching the slide to prevent damage to micropattern areas by using forceps.
Place the 6-well plate face down over the opened blister tray with the chip, flip them over and let the chip fall into the well plate.
Add 2 mL of PBS−/− to the 6-well containing the micropatterned slide, ensuring the slide is completely covered.
Incubate the chip for 2 h at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the chip by adding 4 mL of PBS−/−, swirling gently, then removing a volume of 4 mL.
Repeat washing procedure with PBS−/− five times.
For the last two washing steps, use cell culture medium instead of PBS−/−.
Transfer the chip into the bottom plate of the 1 well CYTOOchamber™ with patterns facing up using tweezers.
Immediately add 1 mL PBS−/− to prevent the micropatterned slide from drying out.
Transfer the chamber into a cell culture dish with lid.
Harvest the cells.
Wash cells with PBS−/−/5 mM EDTA.
Add Trypsin/EDTA solution for 5 min at 37°C (for a 10 cm cell culture dish, use 1.5 mL Trypsin/EDTA).
Stop the reaction by adding 5 volumes of cell culture medium.
Centrifuge cells (200 g, 4 min, 20°C–25°C).
Resuspend cell pellet in 5 ml cell culture medium.
Pass the cells through a sieve with 40 μm pore size to remove large cell clusters and cellular debris.
Count the cells.
Resuspend cells in medium to obtain a cell suspension of 50,000 cells/mL for each cell type.
Mix equal volumes of the two cell types (1 + 1) to generate a cell suspension with a concentration of 50,000 cells/mL.
Aspirate the PBS−/− solution from the chip using a 1,000-μL pipette without touching the surface.
Add 450 μl of mixed cell suspension (22,500 cells in total) to the chip slowly and dropwise.
Incubate the cells for an additional 30 min to allow the cells to settle and spread at the chip surface.
Fill up the CYTOOchamber™ to 2 ml in total with medium.
Incubate again for additional 3 h to ensure complete spreading of the cells.
Extend incubation time for 1–2 hours if cells are not completely attached to the surface of the chip.
Place the CYTOOchamber™ under the microscope.
Heat the incubation chamber to 37°C.
Ensure a constant inflow of 5% CO2.
Set the focus on the cells using the Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) mode of the microscope.
Move around the entire chip by zooming in and out, specifying several Z-positions that will be later successively approached when capturing the microscopy images.
Select 7 Z-positions to optimize focus stability over a period of 15 hours.
Search for suitable coordinates (X and Y position) that could lead to a collision provided that the cells continue to migrate.
Identify two collision partners in close proximity, such as JAM-A KD cells and JAM-A WT cells.
Distinguish cells by their different fluorescent markers.
Start the recording of cell behavior.
Follow the first image acquisition cycle to ensure all positions are approached and focus is correctly set.
Acquire images for 15 hours, taking pictures at 10-minute intervals (90 cycles total).
Determine optimal stripe width for MCF-7 cells (approximately 15 μm diameter) through testing.
For MCF-7 cells, use 5 μm wide stripes as the optimal configuration.
Avoid using 2.5 μm wide stripes due to reduced cell migration efficiency and elongated shapes.
Use wider than 5 μm stripes if collision frequency reduction is necessary but note changes in analysis.
Ensure identical width stripes are used for analyzing collision events.
Fix cells after live cell image acquisition for subsequent immunofluorescence analysis.
Transfer the chip back into a cell culture dish.
Wash the cells with PBS−/−.
Fix in 4% PFA for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Permeabilize the cells for 10 min in PBS−/−/0.5% Triton X-100.
Wash samples 3 times for 5 min with 100 mM glycine in PBS−/−.
Incubate samples with antibody blocking buffer (PBS−/−, 10% FCS, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween 20, 0.02% BSA) for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate samples with primary antibodies (here: anti-LAMP1 (dilution 1:600 in blocking buffer) or anti-β-Catenin (dilution 1:500)) in antibody blocking buffer for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Wash samples 3 times for 5 min with PBS−/−.
Incubate samples with fluorochrome-conjugated secondary antibodies for 2 h at 20°C–25°C (dilution 1:800).
Stain DNA with 4,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI, dilution 1:1000).
Wash samples three times for 5 min each with PBS−/−.
Cover the sample with a drop of Mowiol and embed it with a coverslip.
Allow the sample to harden for 12–16 h at 20°C–25°C.
Take Z-stacks (0.36 μm-intervals) using the 63× Plan-Apochromat oil-immersion objective (LSM800 Airyscan).
Fix samples with paraformaldehyde as organic solvent-based fixation methods result in a loss of EGFP or mCherry fluorescent signals.
Identify cell pairs of interest on live cell samples using a 20× objective lens.
Notice the position(s) of the cell pairs of interest using the coordinates imprinted on the micropatterned chip.
Take confocal sections Z-stacks with the smallest interval possible using a 63× objective.
Fix samples in 5% PFA, 5% glutaraldehyde mixed at a 1:1 ratio with normal growth medium for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Replace fixation solution by 2.5% PFA, 2.5% GLUT in D-PBS (pH7.2); incubate for 4 h at 20°C–25°C.
Wash samples with D-PBS for a total of 3 times, 20 min per wash at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate with 1% osmium tetroxide in double-distilled water for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Wash samples with ddH2O.
Perform 2 washes for 20 min each at 20°C–25°C.
Perform 1 wash for 20 min at 4°C.
Perform block staining for 12–16 h with 0.5% uranyl acetate in ddH2O at 4°C.
Wash samples 2 times for 20 min each with ddH2O at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate samples in 50% EtOH (in ddH2O) for 20 min at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate samples in 70% EtOH for 20 min at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate samples in 90% EtOH for 20 min at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate samples in 96% EtOH for 20 min at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate samples in 99.8% EtOH for 20 min at 20°C–25°C (repeat this step twice).
Incubate samples in propylene oxide (100%) for 5 min at 20°C–25°C; repeat this step once.
Incubate samples with epon-propylene oxide mixtures at 20°C–25°C: epon-propylene oxide 1 + 3 for 1 h, epon-propylene oxide 1 + 1 for 1 h, epon-propylene oxide 3 + 1 for 1 h, epon pure for 1 h.
Add fresh epon pure to samples and place a gelatin capsule above the position of interest on the micropatterned chip; incubate for 12–16 h at 20°C–25°C.
Fill the gelatin capsule with epon.
Allow the epon to polymerize by incubation for 3 days at 60°C.
Incubate the chip-capsule device in a 60°C water bath and then in a 4°C ice bath; repeat step if necessary.
Place the epoxy block under a stereomicroscope and identify the region of interest using the coordinates.
Remove areas of the epoxy block which are outside the region of interest using a razer blade.
Generate serial sections of the cell starting from the basal side of the cell using an ultramicrotome suitable for EM studies.
Ensure the thickness of the sections is 50 nm for optimal resolution.
Exclude cells that are in close contact at the beginning of the observation period from the analysis.
Ensure all analyzed cells have comparable chances of a collision with a neighboring cell.
Set head-to-head migration for 1–2 hours prior to collision as a prerequisite for inclusion in the analysis of collision events.
Check that the type of migratory behavior is dominant during the observation period.
Define an observation period of 7–8 hours during which the cell behavior must have prevailed to be included into one of the four categories of post-collision behavior.
Include only cells on tracks with the same width into the evaluation.
Analyze cell behavior on tracks with 5 μm for MCF-7 cells.
Ensure post-collision cell behavior prevails for at least half of the observing time before attributing it to one of the four CIL categories.
Calculate the proportion in percentage of the dominant type of migratory behavior among all analyzed cell collisions.
Test the values of at least three independent experiments of the same experimental setup for normality using the D’Agostino-Pearson test.
Compare individual migration types between control and GoI cell collision experiments.
Select cells according to criteria similar to those used for CIL analysis for entosis quantification.
Ensure selected cells are not engulfed at the beginning of acquisition but during observation time.
Divide entotic events into two groups based on which partner is the host and which is the engulfed cell.
Calculate the percentage of engulfed cell types in the total entotic events.
Quantify among the entotic events whether the inner cell is fragmentated, undergoes cell division, or escapes.
Analyze cell motility using ImageJ software and TrackMate plugin.
Set algorithm parameters for particle linking: Downsample LoG detector, Diameter 60.000 px, Threshold 0.01, Median filter.
Define linking settings: Linking max Distance 250 px, Gap-closing max distance 100 px, Gap-closing max frame gap 5.
Calculate track displacement as Euclidean distance and convert from pixel to μm.
Calculate mean velocity of the cells as track displacement/total acquisition time in μm/min.
